### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f19ae3a8ebfcc11b90215c8a4845dbe7eb4dd83f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `940622338ca22efb0d0c12aaba984a3472fe911d` — the merge of head `920bb55198dfe44e7bded459f35bf97655d8787b` into base `f19ae3a8ebfcc11b90215c8a4845dbe7eb4dd83f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 940622338ca22efb0d0c12aaba984a3472fe911d && git checkout 940622338ca22efb0d0c12aaba984a3472fe911d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f19ae3a8ebfcc11b90215c8a4845dbe7eb4dd83f 920bb55198dfe44e7bded459f35bf97655d8787b && git checkout -B drift-repro f19ae3a8ebfcc11b90215c8a4845dbe7eb4dd83f && git merge --no-ff 920bb55198dfe44e7bded459f35bf97655d8787b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f19ae3a8ebfcc11b90215c8a4845dbe7eb4dd83f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `e4262fe9e7308c818abc8b9bff18cd61b16b2344`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.ts + ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/cel-list-membership.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-edge-condition-rows.ts
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Owed by the `Clause-②: yes` line alone (the declaration face): no published schema, governed path or narrowing in the diff. This is the lane's in-seat review, run by L1-a, the seat's L1 thread. Inputs: card #36381, the PR body and diff at this head, and os-dev report 7211812962. Check-runs on the head were still running at this reading, so no gate verdict is taken from them here.

### ① Derived judgments

- `@objectstack/formula` gains two entry exports: `listMembershipSource(read, member, contains, filterCompiled = false)` and `type ListSubjectRead` (`index.ts`). RIGHT. Card #36381 asks the builder to call the validator's own helper "rather than restating it", and a cross-package call needs an export. The signature takes `contains: boolean` and an already-literal `member`, which is what the builder has. It does not take the refusal's `==`/`!=` operator.
- The private `listMembershipRewrite` is now `(${listMembershipSource(read, operand, operator === '==', filterCompiled)})`. Read by hand, each arm (filter-compiled, bare, root) produces the old text minus the outer parentheses, and the wrapper adds them back. So the refusal's `rewrite` param is byte-identical. The new `validate-list-equality-36167.test.ts` block pins it for four sites × two operators.
- `listMembershipCel` (app-shell) now delegates, with `bare: !subject.includes('.')`. RIGHT for the builder's subjects: a `record.`/`previous.` read is dotted, and a flattened start condition's field is bare.
- `readListMembership` accepts the four shapes but keeps only those that round-trip through the writer. So an unguarded `record.f != null && V in record.f` no longer reads back as a row, and opens in the raw editor. The changeset and the Acceptance notes both declare this, and the test file names it as a negative.
- `flow-edge-condition-rows.ts` drops its own two membership regexes and reads through `readListMembership`, so the per-site spelling is known in one place. A member that is not a string literal falls through to the remaining patterns, as before.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/36381-…`: `patch` on `@objectstack/formula` and `@object-ui/app-shell`, `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, on both the PR body and the changeset. AGENTS.md rule 3: kind `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. Correct. Nothing a metadata author writes changes; the validator's accept-set and its refusal text are unchanged.

### ③ Boundary flags

- NOT MEASURED locally: the app-shell type-check. Answered by CI's Type Check UI, which must be green on this head before the queue.
- A test file outside the claimed surface (`ObjectValidationsPanel.typedEmptyOps-11894.test.tsx`, one fixture string): a pin following the new spelling, named in the PR body's Tests list. It is not an adjacent defect fix.
- Acceptance note, filter-compiled sites: a sharing rule's `condition` is where the validator prescribes `.contains(…)`, and no host tells the builder the mount is filter-compiled. The same defect class as this card, at a fourth site the card did not list, and unmeasured. The lane seat files it as a follow-up card with a measure-first step, not a drop.
- `open_questions`: none.
- SQL push-down: no query, id materialisation or join in the diff.

**VERDICT: PASS**

### What to change

- `.changeset/36381-…`, first paragraph: "…so the validator and the Studio builders now take one spelling from one place: … `S.contains(…)` where the condition compiles to a query filter." The builders never write the `.contains(…)` arm. No host tells them a mount is filter-compiled, which the PR's own Acceptance note says. Keep the sentence to what the builders write: the `record.`/`previous.` arm and the bare arm. Say that the filter-compiled arm is the validator's alone until a host passes the flag, and name the follow-up card (below) once it is filed.

- Sharing-rule (filter-compiled) mounts not told to the builder: **file it, not dropped.** It is this card's own defect class, the builder and the validator disagreeing for a site, at a fourth site the card did not list. Its reach is unmeasured ("not measured whether the generic sharing-rule form offers list subjects"), so the card opens with that measurement. The seat files it; the changeset sentence above then names it.

### Read and clean at this head

- Shape (`l1-face.mjs --pr 37846`): open, draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #36381`. The card asks for three things. The builder calls the validator's helper. The `checkListEquality` docblock's opening line now names `listMembershipSource`, which was N1. And there is a test at three sites (action row, `previous` null on a create, a record-triggered start condition) that asserts the built text equals the validator's rewrite, is accepted unchanged, and evaluates without a fault on the sparse or null row. All three are delivered, so `Fixes` is right.
- Declarations: `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch` on both packages. The `TIER_DEFAULT` review it owes is 7211851500.
- The one file outside the claimed surface (`ObjectValidationsPanel.typedEmptyOps-11894.test.tsx`) is a fixture string following the new spelling, named in the body's Tests list. It is not an adjacent fix, so the four-condition check does not apply.
- The behaviour change for stored text (an unguarded `record.` membership now opens in the raw editor) is declared in the changeset and the Acceptance notes, and pinned as a negative.
- The private rewrite's byte-identity is pinned for 4 sites × 2 operators against the refusal's own `rewrite` param.
- Not judged yet: CI was still running at this reading, including Type Check UI, which answers the dev's NOT MEASURED app-shell type-check. The floor and the full set are read again on the next head.

### Changeset sentences read (not delegated)

- Paragraph 1: the export line is true. The "one spelling from one place" list overclaims (above).
- Paragraph 2: true against the diff and the engine pins, including the "No such key" fault on a sparse row and a null `previous`, and the bare name written as before.
- Paragraph 3: true; it is the raw-editor negative in the test file.
